sine.title: Sine wave
sine.description: Sine describes a periodic oscillation. As x changes, y varies between −1 and 1.
sine.pointLabel: Position on the sine wave. Use the arrow keys to move the point.

orbit.title: Elliptical orbit
orbit.description: This equation defines an ellipse. The parameters a and b are its semi-axes: they control its width and height.
orbit.pointLabel: Position on the orbit. Use the arrow keys to move the point.

ripples.title: Concentric ripples
ripples.description: The radius r increases with time t. The constant c determines how quickly each ripple expands.

bezier.title: Bézier curve
bezier.description: Four points define this cubic curve. The two inner points control its shape, while t identifies a position along the path.

pendulum.title: Pendulum
pendulum.description: This equation describes an ideal pendulum without friction. θ is the angle, g is gravitational acceleration, and ℓ is the pendulum’s length.

lissajous.title: Lissajous curve
lissajous.description: Two perpendicular oscillations create this figure. The frequencies 3 and 2 determine the pattern traced by the point.
